```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(mgm)

library(ggplot2)
library(missForest) # core imputation package

# ==============================================================================
# Path configuration (edit here; every path below references these)
# ==============================================================================

data_proc_dir  <- here::here('Data', 'Processed')    # intermediate outputs

out_fig_dir    <- here::here('Output', '01-Env-health', 'Figures')

dir.create(out_tables_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# --- 4. Run safety check ---

  msg <- paste0(
    "Column count mismatch!\n",
    "------------------------------\n",
    "Current number of columns: ", current_cols, "\n",
    "Number of new variable names: ", target_cols, "\n",
    "Difference: ", current_cols - target_cols, "\n",
    "------------------------------\n",
    "Check whether the select() statement is missing variables, or new_colnames is defined incorrectly."
  )
  stop(msg)
```

# Data input
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 1: Variable definition, selection and renaming
# ==============================================================================
library(dplyr)
library(missForest)
library(psych)
library(tibble)

# 1.1 Define original variable names (list kept as provided)
e_orig_names <- c("e_city", "e_dist", "e_metro", "e_Bus", "e_wlkgrn", "e_wvgrn", "e_wlkblu", "e_wvblu",
                  "e_facil", "e_Price", "e_work", "e_eduEL", "e_comCen", "e_medAc", "e_alcig", 
                  "e_neiAl", "e_neiLow", "e_neiSoci", "e_themCo", "e_clim", "e_poll", "e_lighting",
                  "e_privacy", "e_narrow", "e_PA", "e_sleep", "e_heaFood", "e_lifestyle", "e_safe")

l_orig_names <- c('l_palgt', 'l_pamed', 'l_pahig', 'l_lgtdur', 'l_meddur', 'l_higdur', 
                  'l_sitdur', 'l_leidur', "l_eathealth", 'l_eatout', 'l_smoking', 
                  'l_drinking', "l_medictest", "l_adaptCop", "l_med_seek", "l_info_seek")

mh_orig_names <- c('m_conc', 'm_wea', 'm_pos', 'm_app', 'm_neg', 'm_est', 'm_res', 'm_eat')
ph_orig_names <- c("p_energy","p_pain","p_medD","p_genH","p_sleep","p_daily","p_work","p_mobility")
sh_orig_names <- c("SS_1","SS_2","SS_3","SS_4","SS_5","SS_6","SS_7","SS_8")
ses_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Edu", "Emp", "Imm", "CD", "DurRes", "LivArea")

# 1.2 Select data
all_vars_for_imputation <- c(e_orig_names, l_orig_names, mh_orig_names, ph_orig_names, sh_orig_names, ses_vars)

# Check that the variables exist
if(!all(all_vars_for_imputation %in% colnames(df))) {
  missing_vars <- all_vars_for_imputation[!all_vars_for_imputation %in% colnames(df)]
  stop(paste("Error: the data frame is missing the following columns:", paste(missing_vars, collapse=", ")))
}

df_analysis <- df[, all_vars_for_imputation]

# 1.3 Rename (build old-to-new name mapping)
# Generate new names
e_item_names <- paste0("E", 1:length(e_orig_names))
l_item_names <- paste0("L", 1:length(l_orig_names))
mh_item_names <- paste0("M", 1:length(mh_orig_names))
ph_item_names <- paste0("P", 1:length(ph_orig_names))
sh_item_names <- paste0("S", 1:length(sh_orig_names))

# Apply the renaming
names(df_analysis)[match(e_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- e_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(l_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- l_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(mh_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- mh_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(ph_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- ph_item_names
names(df_analysis)[match(sh_orig_names, names(df_analysis))] <- sh_item_names

# Reorder (E, L, M, P, S, SES)
core_node_names <- c(e_item_names, l_item_names, mh_item_names, ph_item_names, sh_item_names)
all_vars_clean <- c(core_node_names, ses_vars)
df_analysis <- df_analysis[, all_vars_clean]

message("Variable selection and renaming complete.")

# ==============================================================================
# Step 2: Descriptive statistics of the raw data (pre-imputation)
# ==============================================================================

# Define a generic descriptive-statistics function
get_descriptive_stats <- function(data, label="Stats") {
  
  data_num <- data %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(.)))
  
  # Use psych::describe for basic statistics
  desc <- psych::describe(data_num, na.rm = TRUE) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("Variable") %>%
    dplyr::select(Variable, mean, sd, min, max, skew)
  
  missing_counts <- sapply(data, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
  var_types <- sapply(data, function(x) class(x)[1])
  
  # Merge
  final_tab <- desc %>%
    mutate(
      Missing_N = missing_counts[Variable],
      Missing_Pct = round(Missing_N / nrow(data) * 100, 2),
      Type = var_types[Variable]
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(mean, sd, skew), ~round(., 3))) # keep 3 decimal places
  
  return(final_tab)
}

# 2.1 Ensure SES variables have the right format (for statistics)
ses_factor_vars <- c("Gender", "Emp", "Imm", "CD", "Edu")
df_raw_stat <- df_analysis
for(col in ses_factor_vars) {
  if(col %in% names(df_raw_stat)) df_raw_stat[[col]] <- as.factor(df_raw_stat[[col]])
}

# 2.2 Build and export the raw statistics table
stats_raw <- get_descriptive_stats(df_raw_stat)

# Export CSV
write.csv(stats_raw, file.path(out_tables_dir, "Table_Descriptive_Raw_Data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
message("Raw-data statistics table exported: Table_Descriptive_Raw_Data.csv")

# Print a preview (first few rows)
print(head(stats_raw))

# ==============================================================================
# Step 3: missForest imputation
# ==============================================================================

# 3.1 Prepare data for imputation (categorical variables must be factors)
df_for_imp <- df_analysis
for(col in ses_factor_vars) {
  df_for_imp[[col]] <- as.factor(df_for_imp[[col]])
}

message("\nStarting missForest imputation (ntree=500)... this may take a few minutes...")

# 3.2 Run the imputation
set.seed(123) # fix the random seed for reproducibility
imp_result <- missForest(df_for_imp, 
                         verbose = TRUE, 
                         ntree = 500,     
                         maxiter = 10)

# Extract the imputed data
df_clean <- imp_result$ximp

# 3.3 Print the error report
message("\nImputation complete. OOB error estimate:")
print(imp_result$OOBerror)

# ==============================================================================
# Step 4: Pre/post-imputation comparison report
# ==============================================================================

# 4.1 Build the post-imputation statistics table
stats_imp <- get_descriptive_stats(df_clean)

# 4.2 Merge for comparison
comparison_table <- stats_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, Raw_Mean = mean, Raw_SD = sd, Raw_Skew = skew, Missing_N) %>%
  left_join(
    stats_imp %>% dplyr::select(Variable, Imp_Mean = mean, Imp_SD = sd, Imp_Skew = skew),
    by = "Variable"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_Diff = round(Imp_Mean - Raw_Mean, 4),
    SD_Diff = round(Imp_SD - Raw_SD, 4)
  )

# 4.3 Export the comparison table
write.csv(comparison_table, file.path(out_tables_dir, "Table_Imputation_Check.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
message("Pre/post-imputation comparison table exported: Table_Imputation_Check.csv")

# 4.4 Check for large changes (warn if a mean shifts by more than 0.5)
large_changes <- comparison_table %>% filter(abs(Mean_Diff) > 0.5)
if(nrow(large_changes) > 0) {
  message("Warning: the following variables show a large mean change after imputation, please check:")
  print(large_changes$Variable)
} else {
  message("Check passed: no large mean shift between pre- and post-imputation.")
}

# ==============================================================================
# Step 5: Final output (prepare for the next splitting step)
# ==============================================================================

for(col in colnames(df_clean)) {
  if(is.factor(df_clean[[col]])) {
    df_clean[[col]] <- as.numeric(as.character(df_clean[[col]]))
    if(any(is.na(df_clean))) stop("Numeric conversion introduced NA")
  }
}

message("\nReady. df_clean is now a complete numeric data frame with no missing values.")
message("Continue with the Step 4 (data splitting) code.")
```


# advanced data process-df_clean
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Step 4: Data forking (SES dummy-variable control, fixed)
# ==============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

message("\n[Step 4] Running data forking (SES type-corrected version)...")

# --- 1. Variable definitions ---

all_items <- c(e_item_names, l_item_names, mh_item_names, ph_item_names, sh_item_names)
ses_vars <- c("Age", "Gender", "Edu", "Emp", "Imm", "CD", "DurRes", "LivArea")

# Group A: treated as continuous numeric (includes low-to-high ordinal variables such as Edu)
ses_numeric_vars <- c("Age", "Edu", "DurRes", "LivArea") 

# Group B: must be treated as categorical factors (nominal + binary variables)
ses_factor_vars <- c("Gender", "Emp", "Imm", "CD")

# --- 2. Prepare the SES data frame (for lm regression) ---

ses_df_model <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(ses_vars)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ses_numeric_vars), ~as.numeric(as.character(.)))) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ses_factor_vars), ~as.factor(.)))

str(ses_df_model)

# --- 3. Prepare the item data ---
df_clean_num <- as.data.frame(df_clean) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(all_items), ~as.numeric(as.character(.))))


# --- 4. Run the forking ---

# === Branch A: df_raw_bggm (for BGGM) ===
df_raw_bggm <- df_clean_num 
message("df_raw_bggm ready.")


# === Branch B: df_resid (for DAG) ===
df_resid <- df_clean_num # copy the structure

message("Computing residuals (dummies handled automatically)...")

for(item in all_items) {
  tmp_data <- cbind(Y_Target = df_clean_num[[item]], ses_df_model)
  
  fit <- lm(Y_Target ~ ., data = tmp_data, na.action = na.exclude)
  
  df_resid[[item]] <- residuals(fit)
}

message("df_resid ready (SES categorical variables correctly controlled).")


# --- 5. Compute composite scores ---
calc_score <- function(data, vars) {
  if(length(vars) == 0) return(rep(NA, nrow(data)))
  rowMeans(data[, vars, drop=FALSE], na.rm=TRUE)
}

df_scores <- df_resid %>%
  mutate(
    E_Score = calc_score(., e_item_names),
    L_Score = calc_score(., l_item_names),
    M_Score = calc_score(., mh_item_names),
    P_Score = calc_score(., ph_item_names),
    S_Score = calc_score(., sh_item_names),
    H_Score_Total = rowMeans(cbind(M_Score, P_Score, S_Score), na.rm=TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(E_Score, L_Score, M_Score, P_Score, S_Score, H_Score_Total), ~as.numeric(scale(.))))

message("df_scores ready.")

# ==============================================================================
# Save
# ==============================================================================
continuous_items <- c() 

save(df_clean_num, df_raw_bggm, df_resid, df_scores, 
     ses_df_model,
     continuous_items,
     file = file.path(data_proc_dir, "Data_Forked_Step4.RData"))

message("\nData updated and saved to Data_Forked_Step4.RData")


```

# Bootnet stability analysis for all models
```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# III. PHASE 3: STABILITY ANALYSIS (bootnet) - Updated for SES-Adjusted Residuals
# ==============================================================================
# 1. Use EBICglasso as a fast proxy for BGGM in the stability test.
# 2. Important: use df_resid (from Step 4), because SES effects have already been removed.

library(bootnet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

message("\n🚀 STARTING PHASE 3: STABILITY ANALYSIS FOR ALL MODELS")

# 1. Basic configuration and checks
if(!exists("out_dir")) out_dir <- out_fig_dir
if(!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Key check: ensure df_resid exists
if(!exists("df_resid")) {
  stop("Error: 'df_resid' not found. Run the Step 4 code first to generate the deconfounded residual data.")
}

# Loop: Mental -> Physical -> Social
for(model_label in names(multi_models)){
  
  message(paste("\n----------------------------------------------------"))
  message(paste(">>> [Phase 3] Testing Stability for:", model_label))
  message(paste("----------------------------------------------------"))
  
  # 2. Prepare data
  nodes_extra <- multi_models[[model_label]]
  target_vars <- c(e_names, l_names, nodes_extra)
  
  data_for_boot <- df_resid %>% dplyr::select(all_of(target_vars))
  
  # 3. Define bridge communities dynamically
  n_e <- length(e_names)
  n_l <- length(l_names)
  n_h <- length(nodes_extra)
  
  communities <- list(
    "Environment" = 1:n_e,
    "Lifestyle"   = (n_e + 1):(n_e + n_l),
    "Health"      = (n_e + n_l + 1):(n_e + n_l + n_h)
  )
  
  # 4. Run bootnet
  # 4.1 Estimate the base network (EBICglasso)
  message(paste("   👉 Estimating base network (EBICglasso on Residuals)..."))
  
  network_estimate <- estimateNetwork(
    data_for_boot, 
    default = "EBICglasso", 
    corMethod = "cor", 
    tuning = 0.5,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  # 4.2 Run case-dropping bootstrap
  message(paste("   👉 Running 1000 bootstraps (this takes time)..."))
  # Fix the bootnet seed
  set.seed(777)
  
  boot_res <- bootnet(
    network_estimate, 
    boots = 1000,              # 1000 recommended for a full run
    type = "case",             # case-dropping method
    statistics = c("bridgeExpectedInfluence"), # test Bridge EI only
    communities = communities, # pass the dynamic communities
    nCores = 8,                # multi-core speedup (adjust to your machine)
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  # 5. Compute the CS-coefficient
  # cor = 0.7 is the standard threshold (CS > 0.25 acceptable, > 0.5 excellent)
  cor_stab <- corStability(boot_res, cor = 0.7)
  cs_value <- cor_stab[1] # extract the CS value for Bridge EI
  
  message(paste("   📊 CS-coefficient (Bridge EI):", round(cs_value, 3)))
  
  # 5. Plot and save
  pdf_filename <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("Stability_CS_", model_label, ".pdf"))
  pdf(pdf_filename, width = 10, height = 6)
  
  p <- plot(boot_res, statistics = "bridgeExpectedInfluence") + 
    ggplot2::labs(title = paste("Stability of Bridge EI -", model_label),
         subtitle = paste("CS-coefficient (cor=0.7) =", round(cs_value, 3)),
         caption = "Criteria: CS > 0.25 is acceptable; CS > 0.5 is stable.") + 
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face="bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  
  message(paste("   ✅ Saved plot to:", basename(pdf_filename)))
}

message("\n🎉 PHASE 3 ALL COMPLETED! Check your output folder.")
```




# Analysis 3: DAG three steps
```{r}

library(bnlearn)
library(bootnet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ==============================================================================
# IV. PHASE 2: DAG ANALYSIS (Based on SES-Adjusted Residuals)
# ==============================================================================
message("\n🚀 STARTING PHASE 2: DAG ANALYSIS")

# Ensure output directories exist
if(!exists("out_dir_dag")) out_dir_dag <- file.path(out_dir, "DAG_Analysis")
if(!dir.exists(out_dir_dag)) dir.create(out_dir_dag, recursive = TRUE)

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 1: Core computation and raw-object save (computation & save raw RDS)
# ==============================================================================

message("\n🚀 [Step 1] STARTING HEAVY COMPUTATION (Bootstrap on Residuals)")
message(paste("📂 Output Directory:", out_dir_dag))

# Check that df_resid exists
if(!exists("df_resid")) stop("Error: df_resid does not exist. Run Step 4 first.")

target_models <- names(multi_models) 

for(model_label in target_models){
  
  message(paste(">>> [Computing] Running Bootstrap for:", model_label))
  
  # --- A. Data preparation (using the deconfounded residuals) ---
  nodes_extra <- multi_models[[model_label]]
  node_names_model <- c(e_names, l_names, nodes_extra)
  
  dat_resid_sub <- df_resid %>% 
    dplyr::select(all_of(node_names_model))
  
  # --- B. Blacklist setup (tiered blacklist) ---
  # Forbid: Lifestyle -> Environment
  # Forbid: Health    -> Environment
  
  non_env_nodes <- c(l_names, nodes_extra)
  
  black_list <- expand.grid(from = non_env_nodes, to = e_names, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  # --- C. Core computation (bootstrapping) ---
  tryCatch({
  # Fix the DAG bootstrap seed
    set.seed(999)
    
    start_time <- Sys.time()
    
    # Core computation: R=500 (raise to 500 or 1000 for stable results), alpha=0.01
    # Use the PC-stable algorithm
    str_fit <- boot.strength(
      data = dat_resid_sub, 
      R = 500,    # <--- recommendation: use 500 or 1000 for publication
      algorithm = "pc.stable",
      algorithm.args = list(
        blacklist = black_list, 
        alpha = 0.01  # significance level
      )
    ) 
    
    end_time <- Sys.time()
    duration <- round(difftime(end_time, start_time, units = "secs"), 1)
    message(paste("   ⏱️ Computation finished in", duration, "seconds."))
    
    # --- D. Save the raw object (.rds) ---
    rds_filename <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Boot_Object_", model_label, ".rds"))
    saveRDS(str_fit, file = rds_filename)
    
    message(paste("   💾 Saved Raw RDS:", rds_filename))
    
  }, error = function(e){
    message(paste("   ❌ Error in calculation for", model_label, ":", e$message))
  })
}

message("\n✅ [Step 1] ALL COMPUTATIONS DONE. Raw data saved to .rds files.")
message("👉 Next: Run 'Step 2' (Sensitivity) and 'Step 3' (Plotting).")

```



```{r}
library(bnlearn)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) # ggplot2 is used for the line plot

library(bnlearn)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2) 

# ==============================================================================
# STEP 2: Sensitivity analysis (with CSV export and elbow plot) - extended
# ==============================================================================

message("\n📊 [Step 2] STARTING SENSITIVITY CHECK & PLOTTING")

# Define the test range
test_thresholds <- sort(unique(c(seq(0.70, 0.95, by = 0.05), 0.98)))

# Define the thresholds for which a CSV should be exported
export_targets <- c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90, 0.95)

target_models <- names(multi_models)

for(model_label in target_models){
  
  # --- 1. Read the RDS file saved in Step 1 ---
  rds_file <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Boot_Object_", model_label, ".rds"))
  
  if(!file.exists(rds_file)){
    message(paste("⚠️ Skipped:", model_label, "(RDS file not found)"))
    next
  }
  
  message(paste("\n>>> Analyzing Model:", model_label))
  str_fit <- readRDS(rds_file)
  
  # --- 2. Loop over thresholds and count edges ---
  results_list <- list()
  
  for(th in test_thresholds){
    # Compute the averaged network
    avg <- averaged.network(str_fit, threshold = th)
    # Count the edges
    final_arcs <- as.data.frame(avg$arcs)
    num_edges <- nrow(final_arcs)
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # If this is a target threshold (85, 90, 95), save a CSV immediately
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    if(th %in% export_targets){
      # example filename: DAG_Arrows_0.9_Mental_Health.csv
      arrow_file <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("DAG_Arrows_", th, "_", model_label, ".csv"))
      
      if(num_edges > 0){
        write.csv(final_arcs, arrow_file, row.names = FALSE)
        message(paste0("      💾 [Export] Saved arrows for threshold ", th, " (Edges: ", num_edges, ")"))
      } else {
        message(paste0("      ⚠️ [Export] Threshold ", th, " has 0 edges, skip saving."))
      }
    }
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Auto-generate a description (for reference only)
    desc <- ""
    if(num_edges > 100) desc <- "Very Dense"
    else if(num_edges > 50) desc <- "Dense"
    else if(num_edges >= 20) desc <- "Moderate (Interpretable)"
    else if(num_edges > 5) desc <- "Sparse (Skeleton)"
    else desc <- "Very Sparse"
    
    # Store in the list
    results_list[[as.character(th)]] <- data.frame(
      Threshold = th,
      Edge_Count = num_edges,
      Description = desc,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  # Combine into a data frame
  df_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
  
  # --- 3. Export the summary CSV (for the supplement) ---
  csv_name <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Sensitivity_Table_", model_label, ".csv"))
  write.csv(df_results, csv_name, row.names = FALSE)
  message(paste("   💾 Summary Table Saved:", csv_name))
  
  # --- 4. Draw the line plot (scree plot) ---
  p <- ggplot(df_results, aes(x = Threshold, y = Edge_Count)) +
    geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.2) +
    geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Edge_Count), vjust = -0.8, size = 3.5) +
    # Mark the 0.85 and 0.90 positions
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.85, 0.90, 0.95), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = test_thresholds) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Sensitivity Analysis:", model_label),
      subtitle = "Number of Edges vs. Inclusion Threshold",
      x = "Threshold (Bootstrap Confidence)",
      y = "Number of Edges (Complexity)"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 11)
    )
  
  plot_name <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Sensitivity_Plot_", model_label, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(plot_name, plot = p, width = 8, height = 6)
  message(paste("   📈 Plot Saved:", plot_name))
}

message("\n✅ [Step 2] Analysis Done.")
message("👉 Checked Output folder for new 'DAG_Arrows_0.XX_....csv' files.")
```

# DAG_Spring_plot
```{r}
library(qgraph)
library(dplyr)
library(bnlearn)


# STEP 3: Final plotting (free layout + high-repulsion comparison)


FINAL_THRESHOLD <- 0.70 # or 0.90

# Labels
param_label_1 <- paste0("Threshold: ", FINAL_THRESHOLD, " | Layout: High Repulsion Spring")
param_label_2 <- "Green: Forward | Red: Feedback | Gray: Within-Group"

message(paste("\n🎨 [Step 3 Contrast] STARTING FORCE-DIRECTED PLOTTING | Threshold:", FINAL_THRESHOLD))

target_models <- names(multi_models) 

for(model_label in target_models){
  
  # --- 1. Read the raw data (unchanged) ---
  rds_file <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("Boot_Object_", model_label, ".rds"))
  
  if(!file.exists(rds_file)){
    message(paste("⚠️ Skipped:", model_label, "(RDS not found)"))
    next
  }
  
  str_fit <- readRDS(rds_file)
  
  # --- 2. Filter edges ---
  avg_dag <- averaged.network(str_fit, threshold = FINAL_THRESHOLD)
  final_arcs <- as.data.frame(avg_dag$arcs)
  all_nodes <- nodes(avg_dag) 
  n_total <- length(all_nodes)
  
  # --- 3. Prepare matrices ---
  dag_adj <- matrix(0, nrow = n_total, ncol = n_total)
  rownames(dag_adj) <- colnames(dag_adj) <- all_nodes
  
  edge_col_mat <- matrix("black", nrow = n_total, ncol = n_total)
  rownames(edge_col_mat) <- colnames(edge_col_mat) <- all_nodes 
  
  # Group-assignment helper function
  get_group_id_safe <- function(node_name_clean){
    e_names_safe <- make.names(e_names)
    l_names_safe <- make.names(l_names)
    if(node_name_clean %in% e_names || node_name_clean %in% e_names_safe) return(1)
    if(node_name_clean %in% l_names || node_name_clean %in% l_names_safe) return(2)
    return(3) 
  }
  
  # --- 4. Fill matrices & colour edges ---
  if(nrow(final_arcs) > 0){
    for(i in 1:nrow(final_arcs)){
      f <- final_arcs[i, "from"]
      t <- final_arcs[i, "to"]
      
      if(f %in% all_nodes && t %in% all_nodes){
        dag_adj[f, t] <- 1
        
        g_src <- get_group_id_safe(f)
        g_dst <- get_group_id_safe(t)
        
        if(g_src == g_dst) edge_col_mat[f, t] <- "gray80"       
        else if(g_src < g_dst) edge_col_mat[f, t] <- "forestgreen" 
        else edge_col_mat[f, t] <- "firebrick2"  
      }
    }
  }

  # --- 5. Define communities (keep the index logic) ---
  group_ids <- sapply(all_nodes, get_group_id_safe)
  idx_e <- which(group_ids == 1)
  idx_l <- which(group_ids == 2)
  idx_h <- which(group_ids == 3)
  
  groups_list <- list("Environment" = idx_e, "Lifestyle" = idx_l)
  groups_list[[model_label]] <- idx_h 
  
  my_colors <- c(
    if("Environment" %in% names(custom_node_colors)) custom_node_colors["Environment"] else "#A6CEE3",
    if("Lifestyle" %in% names(custom_node_colors)) custom_node_colors["Lifestyle"] else "#B2DF8A",
    if(model_label %in% names(custom_node_colors)) custom_node_colors[model_label] else "#FB9A99"
  )

  # --- 6. Plot (free layout) ---
  tryCatch({
    pdf_name <- file.path(out_dir_dag, paste0("DAG_Spring_", model_label, ".pdf"))
    
    pdf(pdf_name, width = 32, height = 16)
    
    qgraph(dag_adj, 
           layout = "spring",
           layout.par = list(
             repulsion = 3.0,      # repulsion: very strong (default ~1), pushes nodes far apart
             area = n_total^3.5,   # area: large, lets nodes spread out fully
             cool.exp = 1.1,       # cooling exponent
             niter = 5000          # iterations: run longer for a more stable structure
           ),
           
           rescale = TRUE,
           
           # === Style (unchanged) ===
           edge.color = edge_col_mat, 
           groups = groups_list,
           color = my_colors, 
           labels = colnames(dag_adj), 
           
           vsize = 2.5,
           label.cex = 0.8,
           
           border.color = "gray30",
           nodeNames = NULL,
           legend = TRUE, 
           legend.cex = 0.5,
           
           directed = TRUE,
           mode = "direct",
           esize = 1.2,
           asize = 2.0,
           
           curve = 0.3,     
           curveAll = TRUE, 
           
           title = paste("DAG Structure (Free Spring Layout):", model_label),
           title.cex = 1.6,
           mar = c(9, 5, 5, 3)
    )
    
    mtext(param_label_1, side = 1, line = 3, adj = 0, cex = 0.85, col = "gray40", font = 3)
    mtext(param_label_2, side = 1, line = 4.5, adj = 0, cex = 0.85, col = "gray40", font = 3)
    
    dev.off()
    message(paste("   ✅ Spring Layout Plot Saved:", model_label))
    
  }, error = function(e){
    message(paste("   ❌ Error:", e$message))
    if(dev.cur() > 1) dev.off()
  })
}
```
